page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and support for vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 capability. System memory total is 16.0 GB, yielding a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread compute capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2101.0 and a stress-ng single-core performance of 3079.47 placing the instance in the upper quartile of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance operates within average performance bands, recording a PassMark CPU score of 7553.4 and stress-ng multi-core score of 6156.76. Application-level performance shows web serving throughput of 6.43 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 5.92 million operations per second. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures lower at 37.93 GB/sec, reflecting a constraint under heavy memory-bound execution.

The combination of dedicated CPU cores, balanced memory, and direct local NVMe storage offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for general applications needing fast disk access without high dedicated hardware overhead. The resource configuration is well suited for web servers, microservice API backends, caching layers, small relational databases, and light text processing tasks. Compute workloads requiring heavy multi-threaded compilation or large LLM inference perform less effectively on this profile.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM and 236 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with top-tier single-core CPU scores in stress-ng and Geekbench. Multi-threaded processing and web serving throughput demonstrate steady mid-tier capability, achieving 5.92 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.43 GB/sec static web throughput. Read memory bandwidth is lower relative to core performance, making the instance most effective for web serving, microservices, lightweight databases, and general enterprise workloads needing direct local disk speed without requiring heavy memory bandwidth or GPU acceleration.
